clue.text: Shattered crash-test cars OK in this disadvantaged area

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Wrecked test vehicles lie around a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' is the anagram signal working on CRASHTESTCARSOK; 'in' is a link, and 'this' points back to the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the wrong side of the tracks comes from the poorer part of town, an idiom from railway-divided American towns.

clue.text: Cunningly we reinstall a source of water

indicators.note: done cunningly suggests artful rearrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A plumber slyly puts back the water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' rearranges WEREINSTALLA; the 'a' that looks like part of the definition belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is a bore where groundwater rises under its own pressure, so it supplies water.

clue.text: Turning up in cab, murder dance!

indicators.note: Turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dramatic headline: a killing in a taxi, then a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link, but it is what signals the hidden word. 'Turning up' (a down clue) reverses ABMUR to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Dumping ground, aim of metrication fanatics?

definitions.meaning: those keen on metres want to abolish the imperial yard

explanation.surface: A tip, and what people pushing the metric system want.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a verb and a noun: scrap the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is a site where discarded metal and junk are left, so it is a place for dumping.

clue.text: Mischievous brats ultimately admit mistakes

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the closing letter of admit

parts.note: errors are mistakes

explanation.surface: Naughty children finally own up to their misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Little terrors is the stock phrase for unruly children, so the word covers naughty kids.

clue.text: Artist and composer ignoring a writer from Italy

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter a is dropped from the composer

parts.note: Edward Elgar, English composer
Umberto Eco, Italian novelist

explanation.surface: Introducing a painter and a musician who skip over an Italian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring a' drops an A from ELGAR to leave ELGR.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: With one being admitted, pause exam

indicators.note: being admitted means let in, so one goes inside the pause

parts.note: a rest is a pause
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A break is allowed, then the test resumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a retaken examination, so it is a kind of exam.

clue.text: Caught skinny rat washing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
lean means skinny
to rat is to inform on someone, to sing

explanation.surface: A thin rodent is captured mid-bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a verb here: to betray, as does 'sing' in criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing is the act of making clean, synonymous with washing.

clue.text: In retrospect transfer person recording speeds, say

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the synonym is read backwards

parts.note: to remit is to transfer money

explanation.surface: Looking back, a money transfer is linked to someone noting speeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer clocks how fast competitors go, with speeds just one example of what such an official measures.

clue.text: Record entry about fierce beast returning around start of summer

indicators.note: around means the reversed letters surround the first letter of summer
returning means going back, so about plus the beast are read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a tiger is a fierce beast

indicators.note: start of means take the opening letter of summer

explanation.surface: A diary note about a tiger coming back early in the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RETIGER into REGITER, and 'around' wraps that round S.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to enter something formally into a record, matching the verb phrase.

clue.text: Surprising solicitation for one promoting alliances

indicators.note: surprising suggests something unexpected, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unexpected request from someone keen on partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalitionist advocates coalitions, which are alliances of parties or groups.

clue.text: Cleanser's bogus power over heart of pathogens

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: sham means bogus
P is the physics abbreviation for power
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: heart of means the central letter of pathogens

explanation.surface: A sanitiser is a fake, powerless against germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a positional link, but it is the cricket abbreviation O, an over being a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap for hair or carpets, so it is a type of cleaning agent.

clue.text: Some treat in Torquay to use up profits, maybe

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words

explanation.surface: A seaside indulgence in a Devon resort that dents a business's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into something is to consume part of it, with profits a typical thing that gets reduced.

clue.text: Region circling northern sphere of action

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so region goes round northern

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: A district wrapped around the north where things happen.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is figuratively a field of activity, a scene where things are done.

clue.text: Sorted out exit terms for hardliner

indicators.note: sorted out means arranged afresh, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Negotiated departure conditions for an uncompromising figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds uncompromising views, which is what a hardliner does.

clue.text: Small cry of grief mostly, before oddly terminable kangaroo court, say

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the cry

parts.note: a howl is a cry of grief

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of terminable

explanation.surface: A little wail of sorrow comes before a court whose proceedings could be ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is a sham tribunal with a fixed verdict, just like a staged political trial.

clue.text: Musical character left cycling round upset old hag

indicators.note: round means the cycled word goes around the reversed hag
cycling means a letter goes round from one end to the other

parts.note: taken as the word left

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a crone is an old hag

explanation.surface: A cyclist going left swerves round an old woman who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves a letter from the end of left to its front; 'upset' suits a down clue, where reading backwards means upwards. 'character' means a printed symbol, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is a symbol on the musical stave, so the tenor clef is a musical character in the printing sense.

clue.text: Reserved comedian, essentially shy and strained

parts.note: a wit is a comedian

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, the central letter of shy

parts.note: drawn means strained, tired-looking

explanation.surface: A quiet comic who is timid and tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawn and reserved both describe someone shy and uncommunicative.

clue.text: A row about English student's workroom

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a row
L, a learner, is a student; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning an English student's study room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here, a tier of seats, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a room for working.

clue.text: Type of contract US Democrats would appreciate?

definitions.meaning: in bridge, a ... contract is bid without a trump suit
read as ..., the absence of Donald Trump

explanation.surface: A deal that America's opposition party would welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is a card game in which the winning bid, a contract, may be played without trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge contract with no trump suit is one particular kind of bridge contract.

clue.text: Darkest time man on board reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the chess piece is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A grim hour as a crew member's news comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period without daylight, the darkest part of the day.

clue.text: Part of fleet ideally finding helpful current?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ships hope to find a favourable flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'finding' in the definition, but it only links wordplay to definition: 'finding helpful current' cannot stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee tide runs with the wind, so it helps a vessel along; a sailing term.

clue.text: Enraged sea dog beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, the first letter of the sea dog

parts.note: a pirate is a sea dog, a seafaring rogue

explanation.surface: A furious old sailor loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rent trouble? That's potentially destructive

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for the noun: a thing that may cause destruction

parts.note: rent means torn
ado is trouble, fuss

explanation.surface: A dispute over rent could become damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money for housing, but it is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirlwind that can wreck buildings, so it is a thing capable of devastation.

clue.text: Kind of bomb in letter people drop

definitions.meaning: an H-bomb, named after the letter H
the letter H, often dropped in speech ('ouse for house)

explanation.surface: A weapon inside a letter that gets dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is how the letter H is spelt out, the H of H-bomb and of dropped aitches.

clue.text: Rum and Asti I mixed in dessert

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A cook stirs rum and sparkling wine into a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

clue.text: Strip of wood India put together for their police baton

indicators.note: put together means joined, so the strip and the letter are combined

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A wooden strip and India are combined to make a truncheon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to India: a lathi is the long bamboo stick of Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is the heavy stick carried by police in South Asia, their equivalent of a truncheon.

clue.text: Potato father had mashed instantly

indicators.note: mashed means crushed to a pulp, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Dad mashed the potatoes in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: At the drop of a hat is an idiom for without hesitation, immediately.
